title: Omni Keeps the Record
summary: Omni writes on the plates as commanded by his father Jarom.

explicit_facts.text: Omni was commanded by his father Jarom to write on the plates to preserve the genealogy.

unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the plates, writing tool, clothing, and surroundings.

narration.text: Behold, it came to pass that I, Omni

prohibited_inventions: Do not show Jarom unless the scene is explicitly depicting his presence; this verse only reports his command.

title: Omni’s War and Record
summary: Omni reports fighting to defend the Nephites, admits his failures to keep the Lord’s commandments, recalls periods of peace and war, and transfers the plates to Amaron.

explicit_facts.text: Omni fought with the sword to preserve the Nephites from the Lamanites.
Omni says he did not keep the Lord’s statutes and commandments as he ought.
Omni reports seasons of peace and serious war and bloodshed; after 282 years he conferred the plates upon his son Amaron.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Omni may be shown holding or transferring the plates.
unspecified_visual_details: The location, appearance of the combatants, and any specific battle.

narration.text: I fought much with the sword
and I conferred them upon my son Amaron.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The report spans multiple years; do not depict one specific battle as the whole account.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Amaron’s appearance or a particular battle.

title: Amaron Writes
summary: Amaron writes in his father’s book and reports that the more wicked part of the Nephites was destroyed.

explicit_facts.text: Amaron writes in the book of his father.
After 320 years, the more wicked part of the Nephites was destroyed.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Amaron may be shown writing in the record.
unspecified_visual_details: Where Amaron writes and how the destruction occurred.

narration.text: I, Amaron, write

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The destruction is reported, not narrated as a present action.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage a particular destruction or depict its cause.

title: Judgment and Deliverance
summary: The Lord visited the people in great judgment, spared the righteous from perishing, and delivered them from their enemies.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord had led them out of the land of Jerusalem and preserved them from falling into the hands of their enemies.
The Lord would not allow his words to their fathers about keeping his commandments and prospering in the land to go unverified.
The Lord visited them in great judgment, spared the righteous from perishing, and delivered them from their enemies.

reasonable_visual_inferences: People may be shown moving away from unnamed enemies, without specifying how they were delivered.
unspecified_visual_details: The location, the form of the judgment, and the means of deliverance.

narration.text: the Lord did visit them in great judgment;
but did deliver them out of the hands of their enemies.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The earlier departure from Jerusalem is background, not part of the judgment and deliverance occurring here.
The verses do not describe a visible appearance of the Lord.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the enemies as Lamanites or give the unnamed people a name.
Do not invent a visible appearance of the Lord, a specific judgment event, or a means of deliverance.

title: The Plates Pass to Chemish
summary: Amaron delivers the plates to his brother Chemish, who records that he saw Amaron’s final writing made that same day.

explicit_facts.text: Amaron delivered the plates to his brother Chemish.
Chemish saw Amaron’s last writing, made by Amaron’s own hand on the day he delivered the plates.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The brothers may be shown together as the plates are transferred.
unspecified_visual_details: Their appearance, the location, and the physical details of the plates.

narration.text: I did deliver the plates unto my brother Chemish.

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent dialogue between the brothers.

title: Abinadom’s Account of War
summary: Abinadom identifies himself as Chemish’s son. He reports seeing much war and contention between the Nephites and Lamanites and taking many Lamanite lives with his sword in defense of his brethren.

explicit_facts.text: Abinadom is the son of Chemish.
Abinadom saw much war and contention between his people, the Nephites, and the Lamanites.
Abinadom says he took the lives of many Lamanites with his own sword in defense of his brethren.

unspecified_visual_details: Abinadom’s appearance and surroundings.
The location, timing, and appearance of those involved in the reported conflicts.

narration.text: Behold, I, Abinadom, am the son of Chemish. Behold, it came to pass that I saw much war and contention between my people, the Nephites, and the Lamanites; and I, with my own sword, have taken the lives of many of the Lamanites in the defence of my brethren.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Abinadom reports past events; the verse does not place a battle in the scene’s present.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage the reported combat as a new present-tense event.
Do not invent combat details, wounds, blood, or severed body parts.

title: Amaleki Introduces Mosiah
summary: A record of the people is engraved on plates held by kings. Amaleki identifies himself as Abinadom’s son and begins an account of Mosiah, who was made king over the land of Zarahemla and warned to flee the land of Nephi with those who would heed the Lord.

explicit_facts.text: The record of this people is engraved on plates held by the kings according to the generations.
Amaleki identifies himself as the son of Abinadom.
Mosiah was made king over the land of Zarahemla and was warned by the Lord to flee the land of Nephi; those who would heed the Lord were to depart with him into the wilderness.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Amaleki may be shown delivering or recording his account; Mosiah need not appear.
unspecified_visual_details: Amaleki’s surroundings and appearance.
How the warning was conveyed to Mosiah.

narration.text: Behold, I am Amaleki, the son of Abinadom.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Omni 1:11 does not identify its first-person speaker in the supplied text.
Mosiah’s warning and proposed departure are reported, not shown occurring in this scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show Mosiah physically present or depict his departure as already occurring.
Do not depict the Lord or invent the manner of the warning.
Do not attribute Omni 1:11’s first-person statements to Amaleki.

title: Journey to Zarahemla
summary: He did as the Lord commanded. Those who hearkened departed into the wilderness, were led by preachings and prophesyings and continually admonished by the word of God, and eventually came to the land of Zarahemla.
characters: The unnamed person referred to as “he”
Those who hearkened unto the voice of the Lord

explicit_facts.text: He did according as the Lord had commanded him.
Those who would hearken unto the voice of the Lord departed out of the land into the wilderness.
They were led by many preachings and prophesyings and continually admonished by the word of God.
They were led through the wilderness until they came to the land of Zarahemla.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A group traveling through the wilderness can represent the journey.
unspecified_visual_details: The travelers’ number and appearance
The terrain and route
The appearance of the land of Zarahemla

narration.text: And they departed out of the land into the wilderness, as many as would hearken unto the voice of the Lord;
and they were led by many preachings and prophesyings.
until they came down into the land which is called the land of Zarahemla.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The journey unfolds over time; departure, travel, and arrival should not be compressed into one moment.
Being led by the power of the Lord’s arm does not establish a visible arm.
prohibited_inventions: Do not name the travelers or assign them an unstated identity or relationship.
Do not invent spoken words, named preachers, or prophets.
Do not depict a literal divine arm or an unstated divine appearance.

title: The Peoples Meet
summary: Mosiah’s people discover the people of Zarahemla, who rejoice along with Zarahemla because Mosiah’s people brought the plates of brass.

explicit_facts.text: Mosiah’s people discovered the people of Zarahemla.
The people of Zarahemla and Zarahemla rejoiced because the Lord had sent Mosiah’s people with the plates of brass containing the record of the Jews.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The groups may be shown meeting and rejoicing; plates of brass may be visible.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the plates, the precise meeting place, and the people’s clothing.

narration.text: Now, there was great rejoicing among the people of Zarahemla

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a ceremony or words spoken at the meeting.

title: The People of Zarahemla’s Origins
summary: Mosiah discovers that the people of Zarahemla came from Jerusalem during Zedekiah’s captivity, journeyed through the wilderness, crossed the great waters, and settled where Mosiah found them.

explicit_facts.text: Mosiah learned that the people of Zarahemla came from Jerusalem when Zedekiah was carried captive into Babylon.
They journeyed in the wilderness, crossed the great waters by the hand of the Lord, and dwelt in the land where Mosiah discovered them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The account may be presented as narration over the Zarahemla setting, rather than staging the earlier journey.
unspecified_visual_details: The route, means of crossing the waters, and visual details of the journey.

narration.text: they had dwelt there from that time forth.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These verses recount past events, not a new present-tense journey scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Zedekiah or the Babylonian captivity as physically present.

title: A People Without Shared Speech
summary: Mosiah finds the people numerous but unable to understand one another; he causes them to be taught his language, after which Zarahemla gives his genealogy from memory.

explicit_facts.text: The people of Zarahemla had become numerous, endured wars and contentions, had a corrupted language, lacked records, and could not be understood by Mosiah’s people.
Mosiah caused them to be taught his language; Zarahemla then gave his fathers’ genealogy according to memory.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The two groups may be shown attempting to communicate; instruction in Mosiah’s language may be shown.
unspecified_visual_details: The teaching method and appearance of any records beyond the stated plates.

narration.text: Mosiah caused that they should be taught in his language.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses summarize conditions and teaching; do not invent specific conversations.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent dialogue, a written genealogy, or records brought by the people of Zarahemla.

title: The Peoples Unite
summary: The people of Zarahemla and Mosiah unite, and Mosiah is appointed king.

explicit_facts.text: The people of Zarahemla and Mosiah united together, and Mosiah was appointed their king.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The united people may be shown gathered as Mosiah is recognized as king.
unspecified_visual_details: The form of appointment and any regalia or ceremony.

narration.text: Mosiah was appointed to be their king.

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a coronation ritual or dialogue.

title: The Engraved Stone
summary: A large engraved stone is brought to Mosiah, who interprets its engravings by the gift and power of God.

explicit_facts.text: In Mosiah’s days, a large engraved stone was brought to him, and he interpreted the engravings by the gift and power of God.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mosiah may be shown examining or interpreting the engraved stone.
unspecified_visual_details: The engravings’ appearance, the stone’s exact size and material, and who brought it.

narration.text: he did interpret the engravings by the gift and power of God.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a specific supernatural visual effect.

title: The Account of Coriantumr
summary: They gave an account of Coriantumr and the slain of his people. The people of Zarahemla discovered him, and he dwelt with them for nine moons. It also spoke of his fathers, his first parents who came from the tower when the Lord confounded the people's language, the Lord's judgments, and bones scattered in the land northward.

explicit_facts.text: They gave an account of Coriantumr and the slain of his people.
The people of Zarahemla discovered Coriantumr, and he dwelt with them for nine moons.
It spoke briefly of his fathers. His first parents came from the tower when the Lord confounded the people's language.
The severity of the Lord fell upon them according to his judgments, and their bones lay scattered in the land northward.

unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of Coriantumr and the people of Zarahemla
The circumstances of Coriantumr's discovery
The appearance and location of the tower
The account's medium and any present-time setting

narration.text: And they gave an account of one Coriantumr, and the slain of his people.
And Coriantumr was discovered by the people of Zarahemla; and he dwelt with them for the space of nine moons.
It also spake a few words concerning his fathers.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Both verses report past events; they do not establish a present-time setting or identify what “It” refers to.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the reported discovery, dwelling, tower event, or scattered bones as a present-time event.
Do not identify the account's medium as a stone or its words as engravings.
Do not add titles or ancestry labels for Coriantumr or the people of Zarahemla.

title: Amaleki Reports Benjamin’s Reign
summary: Amaleki says he was born in Mosiah’s days, lived to see Mosiah’s death, and that Benjamin, Mosiah’s son, reigns in his stead.

explicit_facts.text: Amaleki was born in the days of Mosiah.
Amaleki lived to see Mosiah’s death.
Benjamin is Mosiah’s son and reigns in his stead.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Amaleki may be shown as the narrator; Mosiah and Benjamin need not appear.
unspecified_visual_details: Amaleki’s appearance and surroundings are unspecified.

narration.text: Behold, I, Amaleki, was born in the days of Mosiah; and I have lived to see his death; and Benjamin, his son, reigneth in his stead.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Mosiah’s death and Benjamin’s reign are reported, not depicted as on-page events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Mosiah’s death or invent a coronation.
Do not portray Mosiah as physically present.

title: War in the Days of King Benjamin
summary: The speaker reports a serious war and much bloodshed between the Nephites and Lamanites in King Benjamin’s days. The Nephites gained much advantage, and Benjamin drove the Lamanites out of Zarahemla.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker says they saw a serious war and much bloodshed between the Nephites and Lamanites in King Benjamin’s days.
The Nephites gained much advantage, and King Benjamin drove the Lamanites out of the land of Zarahemla.

unspecified_visual_details: The appearances of King Benjamin, the Nephites, and the Lamanites are not specified.
The precise location and appearance of the battlefield are not specified.

narration.text: And behold, I have seen, in the days of king Benjamin, a serious war and much bloodshed between the Nephites and the Lamanites.
But behold, the Nephites did obtain much advantage over them; yea, insomuch that king Benjamin did drive them out of the land of Zarahemla.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This verse reports past events; do not stage the combat or expulsion as a new present-tense scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent specific tactics, combatants, or battlefield details.
Do not show wounds, blood, or severed body parts.

title: The Narrator's Intention for the Plates
summary: The narrator has begun to grow old and has no seed. Knowing King Benjamin to be just before the Lord, he says he will deliver the plates to him and exhorts all people to come unto God and believe in good gifts.

explicit_facts.text: The narrator has begun to grow old and has no seed.
The narrator knows King Benjamin to be just before the Lord and says he will deliver the plates to him; the transfer is not narrated.
The narrator exhorts all people to come unto God and believe in prophesying, revelations, the ministering of angels, speaking with tongues, interpreting languages, and all things good.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The aging narrator may be depicted with the plates, without showing their transfer.
unspecified_visual_details: The narrator's precise appearance, the plates' appearance, and the location are unspecified.
King Benjamin's appearance and whereabouts are unspecified.

narration.text: I began to be old;
I shall deliver up these plates unto him,
exhorting all men to come unto God, the Holy One of Israel,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The gifts and the statements about good and evil are teachings, not narrated visible events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the transfer of the plates as having happened.
Do not depict King Benjamin, angels, or miraculous manifestations as present in this scene.

title: Amaleki’s Exhortation to Come unto Christ
summary: Amaleki exhorts his hearers to come unto Christ, partake of salvation and redemption, offer their whole souls, fast and pray, and endure to the end.

explicit_facts.text: Amaleki exhorts his hearers to come unto Christ, partake of salvation and redemption, offer their whole souls, continue fasting and praying, and endure to the end.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Amaleki may be shown speaking as narrator, with no depiction of Christ required.
unspecified_visual_details: The audience and the setting of the exhortation.

narration.text: come unto Christ, who is the Holy One of Israel
and endure to the end;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is an exhortation, not a narrated appearance of Christ.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Christ as visibly present.

title: A Group Sets Out for the Land of Nephi
summary: A large group desiring the land of their inheritance sets out through the wilderness under a strong, mighty, stiffnecked leader; a contention occurs, all but fifty are slain, and the fifty return to Zarahemla.
characters: The leader of the expedition to the land of Nephi
The expedition group to the land of Nephi

explicit_facts.text: A number went into the wilderness to return to the land of Nephi, desiring to possess the land of their inheritance.
Their strong and mighty leader caused contention; all but fifty were slain in the wilderness, and the fifty returned to Zarahemla.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The group may be shown traveling; the reported deaths may be conveyed without gore, or kept off-panel.
unspecified_visual_details: The leader’s name and appearance, the nature of the contention, and how the group was slain.

narration.text: they were all slain, save fifty, in the wilderness
and they returned again to the land of Zarahemla.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The text reports the event; do not invent a specific battle or cause of death.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show gore, wounds, or severed body parts.

title: Amaleki's Closing Statement
summary: A group took many others and journeyed again into the wilderness. Amaleki says his brother went with them and that he has not since known concerning them. He says he is about to lie down in his grave, the plates are full, and he ends his speaking.

explicit_facts.text: They took others to a considerable number and journeyed again into the wilderness.
Amaleki's brother went with them; Amaleki has not since known concerning them.
Amaleki says he is about to lie down in his grave, the plates are full, and he is ending his speaking.

unspecified_visual_details: The travelers' appearances and exact number.
The wilderness's appearance.
Amaleki's surroundings and the plates' appearance.

narration.text: and took their journey again into the wilderness.
And I, Amaleki, had a brother, who also went with them; and I have not since known concerning them.
And I am about to lie down in my grave; and these plates are full.
And I make an end of my speaking.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The journey is reported retrospectively, not staged as a present-tense event.
The travelers' later fate is not given.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the reported departure as a present-tense scene.
Do not invent the brother's name or the travelers' fate.
Do not depict Amaleki's death as an event that has occurred.
